questions.question:
Let the time taken to switch between user and kernel modes of execution be t1
while the time taken to switch between two processes be t2. Which of the
following is TRUE?

options.D: Nothing can be said about the relation between t1 and t2

questions.explanation:
A process switch includes a mode switch plus saving/restoring the full process context (registers, memory map, TLB effects). So it costs more than a mode switch alone.

Answer: [latex]t_1\lt t_2[/latex]

questions.question: A system has 6 identical resources and N processes competing for them. Each process can request atmost 2 resources. Which one of the following values of N could lead to a deadlock?
questions.explanation:
Deadlock is possible when every process holds one less than its maximum and nothing is left: N [latex]\times[/latex] (2 [latex]-[/latex] 1) [latex]\ge[/latex] 6, i.e. [latex]N\ge6[/latex].

Strictly, none of 1, 2, 3, 4 can deadlock (with N = 4, after each holds 1 there are still 2 free). The question is flawed; the official key marks N = 4, the largest choice.

Answer: 4 (as per key)

Which of the following statements are true?
I. Shortest remaining time first scheduling may cause starvation
II. Preemptive scheduling may cause starvation
III. Round robin is better than FCFS in terms of response time

questions.question: In the context of operating systems, which of the following statements is/are correct with respect to paging?

options.A: Paging helps solve the issue of external fragmentation
options.B: Page size has no impact on internal fragmentation
options.D: Multi-level paging is necessary to support pages of different sizes

questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- Any free frame can hold any page, so there is no external fragmentation [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Larger pages waste more space in the last page (internal fragmentation) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- Page tables take memory (and TLB, extra accesses) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Multi-level paging is used to shrink page tables, not to support different page sizes [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: Options 1 and 3

questions.question: Consider a process P running on a CPU. Which one or more of the following events will always trigger a context switch by the OS that results in process P moving to a non-running state (e.g., ready, blocked)?

options.A: P makes a blocking system call to read a block of data from the disk
options.B: P tries to access a page that is in the swap space, triggering a page fault
options.C: An interrupt is raised by the disk to deliver data requested by some other process
options.D: A timer interrupt is raised by the hardware

questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- Blocking system call to read disk: P must wait for I/O [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] moved to blocked state [latex]\text{---}[/latex] always a context switch.
- Page fault for a page in swap space: the page must be read from disk [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P is blocked [latex]\text{---}[/latex] always a context switch.
- Disk interrupt for another process: the OS handles it and makes that process ready, but P can continue running [latex]\text{---}[/latex] not always.
- Timer interrupt: P may still have time left in its slice, or the scheduler may pick P again [latex]\text{---}[/latex] not always.

Answer: Options 1 and 2

questions.question:
Consider a system consisting of [latex]k[/latex] instances of a resource [latex]R[/latex], being shared by [latex]5[/latex] processes. Assume that each process requires a maximum of two instances of resource [latex]R[/latex] and a process can request or release only one instance at a time. Further, a process can request the second instance of the resource only after acquiring the first instance.

The minimum value of [latex]k[/latex] for the system to be deadlock-free is ________. (answer in integer)
questions.explanation:
This is the classic deadlock-avoidance-by-resource-count formula. Each of the [latex]5[/latex] processes needs at most [latex]2[/latex] instances of [latex]R[/latex].

A guaranteed deadlock-free allocation is possible if, even in the worst case where every process is holding one instance and waiting for its second, at least one process can still obtain its second instance and finish (then release both, allowing the rest to proceed in turn).

Worst case: each of the [latex]5[/latex] processes holds [latex](max-1)=1[/latex] instance already, using up [latex]5\times1=5[/latex] instances, and one more instance must be available so that at least one waiting process can get its 2nd instance and complete.

So minimum [latex]k=5\times(2-1)+1=6[/latex].

Answer: 6

questions.question: Consider a computer system with ten physical page frames. The system is provided with an accessse quence [latex](a_{1},a_{2},...,a_{20},a_{1},a_{2},...,a_{20})[/latex], where each [latex]a_{i}[/latex] is a distinct virtual page number. The difference in the number of page faults between the last-in-first-outpage replacement policy and the optimal page replacement policy is ______.
questions.explanation:
LIFO: the first pass gives 20 faults; a1-a9 stay in memory and the 10th frame keeps getting replaced (ends with a20). Second pass: a1-a9 hit, a10-a20 fault (11). Total 31.

Optimal: 20 faults in the first pass and only 10 in the second (it keeps 10 of the pages needed next). Total 30.

Difference = 31 [latex]-[/latex] 30 = 1

Answer: 1

questions.question:
Consider a three-level page table to translate a 39-bit virtual address to a physical address as shown below:

The page size is 4 KB = (1KB =[latex]2^{10}[/latex] bytes) and page table entry size at every level is 8 bytes. A process P is currently using 2 GB (1 GB =[latex]2^{30}[/latex] bytes) virtual memory which os mapped to 2 GB of physical memory. The minimum amount of memory required for the page table of P across all levels is _________ KB
questions.explanation:
2 GB / 4 KB = [latex]2^{19}[/latex] pages. Each page-table page holds 4096 / 8 = 512 = [latex]2^9[/latex] entries.

For the minimum, the pages are contiguous:
- Level 3: [latex]2^{19}/2^9=1024[/latex] pages
- Level 2: 1024 entries [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 pages
- Level 1: 1 page

Total = 1027 pages [latex]\times[/latex] 4 KB = 4108 KB

Answer: 4108

questions.question:
Consider the following solution to the producer-consumer synchronization problem. The shared buffer size is N. Three semaphores empty, full and mutex are defined with respective initial values of 0, N and 1. Semaphore empty denotes the number of available slots in the buffer, for the consumer to read from. Semaphore full denotes the number of available slots in the buffer, for the producer to write to. The placeholder variables, denoted by P, Q, R, and S, in the code below can be assigned either empty or full. The valid semaphore operations are: wait() and signal().

Which one of the following assignments to P, Q, R and S will yield the correct solution?

options.A: P: full, Q: full, R: empty, S: empty
options.B: P: empty, Q: empty, R: full, S: full
options.C: P: full, Q: empty, R: empty, S: full
options.D: P: empty, Q: full, R: full, S: empty

questions.explanation:
Here "full" counts free slots (starts at N) and "empty" counts filled slots (starts at 0).
- Producer: wait for a free slot (P = full), add, then signal a filled slot (Q = empty).
- Consumer: wait for a filled slot (R = empty), remove, then signal a free slot (S = full).

Answer: P: full, Q: empty, R: empty, S: full

questions.question: Consider a main memory with five page frames and the following sequence of page references: 3, 8, 2, 3, 9, 1, 6, 3, 8, 9, 3, 6, 2, 1, 3. Which one of the following is true with respect to page replacement policies First In First Out (FIFO) and Least Recently Used (LRU)?

LRU: 3, 8, 2, 9, 1 (5); 6 replaces 8; 8 replaces 2; 2 replaces 1; 1 replaces 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 9 faults

questions.question:
A file system with 300 GByte disk uses a file descriptor with 8 direct block addresses, 1 indirect

questions.question:
A computer has twenty physical page frames which contain pages numbered 101 through
120. Now a program accesses the pages numbered 1, 2, ..., 100 in that order, and repeats the
access sequence THRICE. Which one of the following page replacement policies experiences
the same number of page faults as the optimal page replacement policy for this program?
questions.explanation:
The pages 1..100 are accessed in a cycle, and memory holds only 20.

LRU and FIFO always evict the page that will be needed soonest in a cyclic pattern, so they fault on every access. Optimal evicts the page used farthest in future, which is the most recently used page.

So MRU behaves exactly like the optimal policy here.

Answer: Most-recently-used

questions.question:
Consider a computer system with multiple shared resource types, with one instance per resource type. Each instance can be owned by only one process at a time. Owning and freeing of resources are done by holding a global lock (L). The following scheme is used to own a resource instance:
 function OWNRESOURCE(Resource R) 
    Acquire lock L // a global lock 
    if R is available then 
        Acquire R        
        Release lock L 
    else
        if R is owned by another process P then        
        Terminate P, after releasing all resources owned by P        
        Acquire R        
        Restart P        
        Release lock L        
        end if
    end if    
end function
Which of the following choice(s) about the above scheme is/are correct?

options.A: The scheme ensures that deadlocks will not occur
options.B: The scheme may lead to live-lock
options.C: The scheme may lead to starvation
options.D: The scheme violates the mutual exclusion property

questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- A process never waits while holding resources (the owner is terminated instead), so there is no circular wait [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] no deadlock.
- Two processes can keep terminating and restarting each other without progress [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] livelock possible.
- A process may be terminated again and again and never finish [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] starvation possible.
- Each resource still has only one owner at a time [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] mutual exclusion is kept.

Answer: Options 1, 2 and 3
